Mobi Just Dropped a Spa on Wheels so Awesome, You’ll Want to Move In
34 photos
Photo: Mobi House
Get ready to explore one of the coolest spa concepts in the mobile habitat market – this brand-new design by one of the top tiny house builders in Europe is not only luxurious and mobile, but also modular, which means it can connect seamlessly to one or even several modular units on wheels with various configurations, to create the ultimate wellness and living space.
You’ve probably seen several Nordic saunas on wheels, one of the newest and most popular trends in the tiny living industry, and you’ve surely experienced glamping tiny home retreats with an outdoor rustic-style bathtub. The question is: have you ever seen a modular habitat on wheels that has both of these amenities enclosed under the same roof?
The brand-new Mobi Modul Spa is exactly that – an innovative and luxurious take on the classic glamping concept that brings together a fully-equipped sauna and a separate bathtub space under the same roof. This is, therefore, much more than a plain sauna on wheels, and different than the typical outdoor bathtub. Ultimately, this is a smart take on the indoor/outdoor design trend that it so popular for tiny homes right now, but with a wellness-centered twist.
Unlike many other mobile sauna designs out there, the Mobi Modul Spa is full-sized, meaning it’s just as big as the other designs in the brand’s Modular series that are intended for full-term accommodation, and that’s already a big plus. The 6.6-meter (21.5 feet) length, paired with a standard tiny house width of 2.5 meters (8 feet) and a four-meter (13 feet) height, makes room for a separate, fully-enclosed sauna, plus a separate indoor/outdoor lounge with a full-size bath.
Photo: Mobi House Exterior cladding combines wood-textured materials with corrugated metal for a modern look that also boosts resilience over time. Extensive glazing is a mandatory part of the winning formula, specifically intended to create the feeling of being outdoors, but from the comfort of a private, warm, and cozy home. Everywhere inside this tiny house, guests will be surrounded by beautiful views and will feel effortlessly connected to nature.
The layout of this unique spa concept is comprised of two separate rooms, so to speak. The indoor/outdoor lounge is the most visible part, surrounded by floor-to-ceiling glass on two sides. It’s a modern-classic lounge with comfortable seating, hooks for hanging clothes, and a custom bookcase with open shelves for storage and decorative display. At the same time, it’s a glamping-style bath area with a huge, rustic-style bathtub with a wooden exterior.
This is the type of bathtub often seen in glamping tiny home resorts, outside on the deck, and sometimes inside the house. By placing it inside the Mobi Modul Spa, guests can enjoy it year-round, during any kind of weather and at any time of the day. Plus, it’s strategically placed to maximize views, for an immersive experience.
Apart from protecting it against the elements, this placement adds the indulging comfort of being at home – including the inviting warmth, practical storage, and plush seating. The storage rack – or bookcase –nearby provides easy access to snacks, drinks, everyday essentials, and personal items. In other words, the idea is to enjoy the pleasure of an outdoor hot tub inside a private space with full comfort and superb views.
Photo: Mobi House A glass door separates this multi-purpose lounge from the sauna, which is fully enclosed and equipped with everything needed for a perfect spa experience. Custom wooden benches with comfortable headrests, an electric heater, and even bespoke multicolored lighting create the most inviting spa environment, a cocoon for relaxation that feels truly luxurious.
Potted plants, decorative artwork, and mood lighting complete the fairytale ambiance of this dual-room spa concept, and, of course, every customer is free to further personalize the style of their own spa. The unit itself boasts 16.5 square meters (177.6 square feet) of floor space, and is fully equipped for connection to on-grid utilities. It sits on the THM 660 Lift &Go trailer by MH Trailers, specifically engineered to allow the trailer to be detached from the module.
The Mobi Modul Spa is awesome on its own, but even better when connected to at least one more modular unit. Mobi launched its Modular Series precisely for flexible, creative projects where two or multiple modules can be connected in various configurations (L-shaped, U-shaped, and more) to suit different scenarios and locations.
This is why the Mobi Modul Spa’s size is so important – it’s meant to connect seamlessly to another modular unit of the same size. In the photo gallery, you can see this new spa module sitting right next to tiny house Croissant, a different model in the Modular Series, boasting a residential configuration. A direct passage makes communication between these two units seamless – no uncomfortable distance between them, yet full privacy for each.
Photo: Mobi House Mobi’s concept of connected living spaces with different configurations opens up endless possibilities for both individual owner and tiny living entrepreneurs. The modular compound comprised of the Mobile Spa and tiny house Croissant can become a wonderful wellness retreat, for instance, combining a separate Spa unit with comfortable accommodation. Any individual owner can also add this structure to their property for the ultimate at-home wellness retreat.
Tiny house Croissant , the model featured in the photo gallery next to the Mobi Modul Spa, is a custom version based on the Modul Sunrise, one of the main platforms in the Mobi Modular Series. It boasts 16.2 square meters (174 square feet) of floor space, and it can accommodate up to four people. The layout features an open lounge in the center, a compact kitchen at one end, a bathroom next to it, and a tiny loft above.
This is just one example, but the Mobi Modul Spa can become part of many different configurations, alongside two or more units from the Modular Series. One of the best part is that each module comes with its own trailer, which means that the owner is able to remove or add modules over time with no hassle – mobility equals flexibility, and the modular design takes it to the next level.
Budget-wise, Mobi’s Modular Series is also one of the smartest options, because owners can start small, with a single unit, and add modules over time, when they’re comfortable with that investment.
Photo: Mobi House Imagine the positive impact this could have for beginner entrepreneurs looking to start a glamping or a small rental business, and the same goes for private owners who could start with a single unit for themselves and eventually expand their habitat for the growing needs of a family.
Better yet, this smart concept is just as much about downsizing as it is about growing over time. Full flexibility means that the owner can eventually resell one or more units from any given configuration, without impacting their main residence on wheels.
It also makes it easier to move or relocate. Plus, this kind of modular unit can stay within the family for several generations, precisely because it’s so flexible in terms of functionality and market value.
Photo: Mobi House The new Mobi Modul Spa looks great next to any other design in the Modular Series and, just as important, they look great in natural environments – contemporary, but perfectly immersed in nature. This is the kind of wellness facility that can be enjoyed anytime, any season, and in full privacy, and it doesn’t get more luxurious than that.

5 Malaise-Era Muscle Cars That Were Quicker Than They Looked
16 photos
Photo: Mecum Auctions
The Malaise Era remains the dark age of American automotive history since it ended unrestricted factory performance and thus the golden age of muscle. But while horsepower dropped significantly during those years, there were still some performance rides that kept American muscle alive.
For American performance enthusiasts, the 1970s started with a bang. That model year, GM lifted its displacement ban on intermediate engines and, along with the rest of the Detroit brands, introduced some of the most powerful factory-built performance models of the era.
However, just three years later, rising insurance rates, new emission regulations, an oil crisis and, last but not least, a switch from gross to net horsepower ratings, had a dramatic impact on the industry and nearly killed off muscle cars .
Until the early 1980s, the American automotive industry went through what automotive journalist Murilee Martin later called (and popularized) the "Malaise Era," a period of emission-driven development that took performance off the list of priorities for most carmakers.
Despite all the drawbacks, several brands continued to deliver some form of performace and, although largely subdued, muscle cars continued to exist. Among those Malaise Era muscle cars were the following five models that didn’t look too muscly but were still decently quick in a straight line.
1974 Chevrolet Chevelle Laguna S-3 454 Photo: Bring a Trailer During the late 1960s and up until 1971, the Chevelle , particularly the performance-oriented SS trim, was one of the most potent and sought-after muscle cars around.
However, for the 1973 model year, the entire model line was redesigned following the new Colonnade styling trend and focusing on emissions and safety.
Because performance was no longer a priority, the SS was now more of an appearance package than a standalone performance model.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Since performance was no longer on the list of priorities, the SS was dropped altogether for the 1974 model year. Nevertheless, the Chevelle lineup did continue to have a strong performer within its ranks.
That strong performer was the Chevelle Laguna S-3, a trim developed for NASCAR homologation, which could be equipped with the optional 454-ci (7.4-liter) Mark IV big-block V8 .
While it didn’t look too sporty despite its NASCAR homologation special status, the Chevelle Laguna S-3 equipped with the 235-hp big block could still run the quarter mile in the low 16s, which, although at least two seconds slower than the golden age Chevelle SS, was pretty quick for a Malaise Era performance ride.
Often forgotten or grossly underrated, the 1974 Chevrolet Chevelle Laguna S-3 454 kept the muscle car torch burning during that dark, emission-friendly-focused era.
1974 Dodge Charger Rallye 440 Photo: Bring a Trailer The Charger debuted in 1966 as a lavish fastback coupe developed specifically to rival AMC’s Marlin in the affordable personal luxury car segment, but in 1968, it was totally redesigned and abandoned personal luxury for a more performance-focused approach.
In 1974, the third-generation Charger, which debuted in 1971 with some serious muscle still on offer, was entering its last year on the market and reached its lowest point in terms of performance.
Nevertheless, there was still a trim that offered more-than-decent performance when equipped with the optional 440 Magnum V8.
Photo: Bring a Trailer That trim was the Rallye, a performance package that debuted in 1972 as a replacement for the iconic R/T.
For the 1974 model year, the Mopar brands were offering the 440-ci (7.2-liter) big-block V8 for the last time and when hiding it under the hood, the Charger Rallye had 275 net hp to play with.
While not as fast as the unchoked 440 Magnum Mopars of 1970 or 1971, the Charger Rallye 440 could run the quarter mile in the high 14-second range, which made it one of the quickest muscle cars of the Malaise Era.
1974 Pontiac GTO Photo: Mecum Auctions Most automotive historians and enthusiasts credit Pontiac with kickstarting the golden age of muscle in 1964 when the carmaker added the GTO performance package to its intermediate Tempest/LeMans range.
Ultra popular from the start, the GTO went on to morph into a standalone model that became one of the most iconic muscle cars of all time.
For 1973, the GM division relegated the GTO to an appearance and handling package for the Colonnade-look LeMans and a year later, it slapped the nameplate on a sportier version of the compact Ventura, the Chevy Nova’s Pontiac-badged twin.
Photo: Mecum Auctions This move drove enthusiasts away from the GTO even further, making the compact model a sales flop and one of the most criticized versions of Pontiac's GOAT.
However, the car wasn’t all that bad. Powered by a 350-ci (5.7-liter) V8 rated at 200 hp, it could still run the quarter mile in the high 15s and low 16s, as shown by multiple independent tests conducted by the era’s most prestigious automotive magazines.
Small and apparently underpowered, this model never looked like it deserved the GTO moniker, but in fact, it one of the most capable muscle cars of the Malaise Era.
1976 Plymouth Volaré Road Runner 360 Photo: Bring a Trailer During the golden age of muscle, Plymouth was one of the brands that produced iconic tire shredders.
The most popular muscle car produced by the Chrysler Corporation division during the late 1960s and early 1970s was, of course, the Road Runner.
Introduced in 1968 as a cheaper, no-frills alternative to the upscale GTX , the Road Runner was a marketing hit that became a muscle car legend.
Photo: Bring a Trailer By the end of the 1975 model year however, Plymouth discontinued the Road Runner as a standalone model and transformed it into an optional package for the compact 1976 Volaré.
While it was not as spectacular as the standalone Road Runners, the Plymouth Volaré Road Runner looked aggressive and performed surprisingly well.
In its most potent guise, it was powered by an optional 360-ci (5.9liter) V8 rated at 170 hp, which allowed it to run the quarter mile in the high 16s. Compared to its predecessors, that was unquestionably slow, but for 1976, it was competitively quick and good enough to the thrill performance enthusiasts who sat behind its steering wheel.
1977 Pontiac Can Am Photo: Mecum Auctions After the disastrous sales flop of the 1974 GTO, Pontiac retired the nameplate and focused on performance in the pony car segment with the Firebird range.
However, for the 1977 model year, the GM division decided to reignite interest in its intermediate lineup with a spiritual successor for the GTO.
Dubbed Can Am, the new model was based on the LeMans Sport Coupe, featured a Grand Prix instrument panel, and was powered by the performance motor found in the Firebird Formula and Trans Am.
Photo: Mecum Auctions That motor was the 400-ci (6.6-liter) Pontiac V8, codenamed W72, which produced 200 hp and gave the Can Am a bespoke shaker hood.
With that engine between its shock towers, the 1977 Pontiac Can Am was tested running the quarter mile in the mid-16-second range, which was more than decent for what was essentially the height of the Malaise Era .
The model actually did very well in terms of sales, with Pontiac receiving over 5,000 orders. However, the division only managed to built a little over 1,370 units due to production issues and discontinued the model.

Volvo's New Factory Worker Is Wheeled and Still in Training
53 photos
Photo: Volvo
Volvo's Ghent facility prepares to welcome a new kind of worker. 1.65 meters (5 feet 5 inches) tall, the AEON humanoid robot weighs 60 kilograms (132 pounds), moves around on wheels, and carries loads no heavier than 10 kilos (22 pounds). For the time being, the newcomer is learning to put components into two fixtures. The kicker here is that humans are teaching it how.
Hardly the automated revolution promised by some of the industry's more enthusiastic futurists, with Elon Musk and the Optimus Gen 3 coming to mind. Volvo, however, wants AEON to become a useful addition to its Ghent complex in Belgium. Developed by Hexagon Robotics, the humanoid robot will specialize in repetitive jobs and physically demanding tasks.
Production use is targeted from the middle of 2027, following a pilot in the first half of next year. Volvo's announcement is a bit awkward, though. Back in October 2026, the Swedish manufacturer confirmed 2,500 job reductions worldwide after reporting a particularly miserable third quarter.
Revenue fell 22.6 percent year over year, with the company recording an operating loss of SEK 5.6 billion while burning through SEK 8.9 billion in free cash flow. Adding insult to injury, Volvo Cars also needs to find another SEK 5 billion in savings. Bringing humanoid workers into production is a hard-to-miss juxtaposition, but robots won't replace human workers anytime soon.
The October 2026 job reductions announcement targets white-collar roles, namely administrative, office, engineering, and management staff rather than production line workers. Alongside the 2,500 white-collar job cuts reported in the Q3 2026 financial update, Volvo stated that it's adapting the blue-collar workforce to match lower sales volumes. Reading between the lines, Volvo has probably made a small bet on reducing a part of its production costs with a bunch of robots.
Photo: Volvo Pretending these announcements have nothing to do with the pressure to reduce manufacturing costs would be naive. Speaking of, there is a wider manufacturing rethink underway. As part of the Q3 2026 financial update, Volvo made it clear that it's concentrating production in five dedicated plants globally.
Volvo is also exploring multi-brand assembly operations with Geely at the Belgian plant and in Chengdu, China. As you're well aware, Geely is the Chinese colossus that calls the shots at Volvo Cars nowadays. Zhejiang Geely Holding Group is presently listed as holding nearly 79 percent of the shares.
Geely owned 100 percent of Volvo Cars between August 2010 and October 2021, with Ford selling the Swedish automaker for a puny USD 1.8 billion. The Chinese overlord reduced its ownership to 82 percent in October 2021, then to 79 in November 2023. On both occasions, it did it to improve stock liquidity while funding growth.
Turning our attention back to the wheeled robots from Ghent, the argument here is that certain factory jobs are better suited for robots, who are particularly good at doing the same operation repeatedly. Auto factories already have plenty of robots, albeit not humanoid. Think industrial arms designed to weld, paint, lift, and install components fast.
The human proportions of the AEON robot allow it to interact with the existing assembly plant environment, while its wheeled base provides mobility, making more sense than legs for much of the factory's floor. Nevertheless, the AEON robot wouldn't mean anything if Volvo employees don't demonstrate tasks to it, allowing the robot to learn how to reproduce those tasks consistently.
After placing components accurately into two fixtures, the humanoid worker will be taught to handle multiple components, navigate the production area, and communicate with the factory's automated systems. In TL;DR form, Volvo is effectively asking Ghent personnel to teach a new colleague how to do a variety of jobs before deciding how much of that work the robot can take on.

By: Northern Miner Staff November 26, 2026
Chile has cleared Marimaca Copper (TSX: MARI; ASX: MC2) to begin early construction work at its namesake copper project near Antofagasta, two days after a unit of Sprott (TSX, NYSE: SII) backed a proposed financing package for construction.
Chile’s National Geology and Mining Service granted the mining-method permit to Marimaca’s subsidiary, Compañía Minera Cielo Azul Limitada. It allows site preparation and bulk earthmoving at the Marimaca Oxide Deposit (MOD) site. Full-scale construction still requires board approval, according to Thursday’s company release .
Receipt of the permit “represents another derisking milestone for the MOD project,” BMO Capital Markets mining analyst Rene Cartier said Thursday in a note. “Marimaca is likely to receive additional sectorial permits in due course, though these are not viewed as critical path items.”
The permit builds on environmental approval granted in November 2025, “allowing for the commencement of the fully funded early works construction activities at the project,” said José Antonio Merino, Marimaca’s managing director in Chile.
13-year mine
The open pit, about 45 km from Antofagasta, would produce an average of 48,000 tonnes of refined copper cathode a year over its first decade. Marimaca put the upfront cost at $587 million (C$834.7 million) and the mine life at 13 years in its 2025 feasibility study.
Sprott Resource Lending Corp.’s investment committee backed a proposed funding package of up to $450 million Tuesday. It includes up to $425 million in senior secured debt and up to $25 million in equity under a non-binding term sheet. The first $100 million of the loan would become available after a construction decision, subject to final agreements, due diligence and other conditions, Marimaca said.
The oxide deposit has measured and indicated resources of 213.5 million tonnes grading 0.40% copper, containing about 853,800 tonnes of copper, according to an August 2025 estimate. It also holds inferred resources of 21.2 million tonnes at 0.29% copper for about 62,200 tonnes of the metal. The measured and indicated resources include proven and probable reserves of 178.6 million tonnes grading 0.42% copper.
Marimaca shares rose 2.4% to C$6.30 Thursday morning in Toronto, valuing the company at about C$854 million ($601 million). The shares have traded between C$5.53 and C$13.49 in the past 52 weeks.

It’s that time of year again; Black Friday approaches! And while the e-bike sales have been pretty good all month, there’s no better day than today to find an amazing deal on a new way around your city (or a fitness e-bike, leisure e-bike, cargo e-bike, etc…)!
A lot of sites will throw a lot of affiliate links at you today for anything they can hawk for a few bucks (this site included from our deals team, probably). But this isn’t that. I’m a professional e-bike rider and tester, and the deals below are only for bikes I actually ride, and for companies I would actually recommend to my own family and friends. Basically, this is the good stuff.
Lectric eBikes
Let’s start with Lectric eBikes, since, as the largest e-bike company in North America, they have long been setting the standard for incredible deals and value in the e-bike industry. I’ve long said that you can’t get better value than here. Sure, you can find lower-priced e-bikes out there, but not at this quality level and with this level of customer support.
Lectric’s sales are usually defined by huge collections of free accessories added to their already low-priced e-bikes, further increasing the value. But this year there are also some legit price drops as well. See all of their Black Friday Sales packages here.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The major standouts for me have always been the XP and XP Lite lines.
The latest of each, the XP4 and the XP Lite3 , offer bundle deals with savings of up to $731 and $257 , respectively. For price drops, you’ll find that both the Lectrix XPLite 2 and the XPTrike2 are marked down to new record-low prices.
I’m also a huge fan of their cargo bike, the Lectric XPedition2 , which has savings of up to $405 thanks to those impressive bundles.
But you should also explore the rest of their deals because just about everything is either marked down or comes with a crazy amount of free accessories that you can’t get for this price any other time of the year!
Ride1Up
Ride1Up is another major value leader in the space, and in fact, I’ve been using the Ride1Up Roadster V3 as my everyday commuter e-bike since the summer.
I’m set to surpass 1,000 miles on it (1,600 km) by the end of the month!
That bike is marked down $100 to just $1,295 right now, making it a major deal for a lightweight, 40 lb (18 kg) commuter e-bike that doubles as a gravel bike. Ask me how I know that it can handle hard off-roading, too!
You can also save $150 on the Vorsa , which is an awesome all-around e-bike with multiple levels for riders who want higher or lower performance.
The new Portola 02 folder is a killer deal at $100 off for just $795 (that’s a crazy price!). If you want to go big and powerful, the Revv1 will crush Super73 and is doing so for $500 off !
Last but not least, the Prodigy V2 Eco is just $1,295 after the $100 deal, which is literally the most affordable Bosch-powered electric bike in the world. The only thing stopping me from buying that bike is that I already have one, though at this price, part of me wonders if I should get a spare for friends to use!
Basically, Ride1Up has a ton of Black Friday Sales going on now, and you can check them all out here .
Monarc Bikes
If you want to go a bit further up the quality ladder to get a more premium e-bike, but you still don’t want to spend $2k+, then you should check out Monarc Bikes . It was founded by Lectric eBikes as an offshoot that could focus on building higher-end models while still leveraging Lectric’s industry heavyweight status to get better pricing. That means the company can offer higher-end e-bikes that rival some of the bike shop brands, while still offering direct-to-consumer pricing, 5-year warranties, and industry-leading local customer support by phone and email.
The two models they’ve launched so far are the urban-focused Tracer and the off-road-optimized Marker, though you better believe they’ve got more interesting stuff coming, likely next year. For now, though, these two models cover most folks’ needs and come with higher-end parts like quad-piston hydraulic disc brakes, reverse arch forks, Bafang’s powerful motors, large batteries, and impressive add-ons like rear-facing radar to keep tabs on approaching cars.
The company started by selling e-bikes that came with a free spare battery, but has recently opened up options for single or even no-battery bikes, meaning if you previously bought a Monarc model and already have that free spare battery, you can save a bunch of money by buying only the bike and using your spare battery across the line. Yep, it’s like the power drill model!
You can see all of the sales and deals here!
JackRabbit
JackRabbit may be a bit of a divisive brand due to how different the bikes look, but I freakin’ love these things! By Alex Lennane
26 November 2026
Is it the beginning of the end for airfreight’s new best friend? Following new US export controls, Nvidia has reportedly told its manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers containing its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia.
According to the UK Financial Times today, citing three sources, manufacturers including Dell and Supermicro have told buyers in the four countries that Nvidia will not allow their orders to ship.
It was unclear how long the halt would last – none of the companies has issued a comment.
Nikkei Asia had already reported that at least two Nvidia server partners had suspended shipments to South-east Asian customers, with one also pausing orders from new customers in the region. The reports did not quantify the cargo affected or identify which shipments had been booked to fly.
The uncertainty is also affecting financing. Bloomberg reported that banks had paused a $480m loan to fund purchases of Nvidia GPUs for a data centre in Malaysia.
Since 19 November, the US has required licences for shipments of certain advanced chips subject to its export controls to those four South-east Asian countries and Brazil. The rules can cover some foreign-made chips and include an exclusion for qualifying US-headquartered end users or consignees, or those with a US-headquartered ultimate parent.
Separate provisions target overseas data centres supplying significant computing power to certain restricted users.
Washington also moved this week to add seven companies to its Entity List, including those linked to Nvidia partner Megaspeed, citing the risk of diversion. Malaysia said it would advise its data centre operators against hosting or providing services to the listed companies.
The US move came on the day Nvidia announced Jensen Huang’s return as chief executive. He is due to testify before the US Senate Banking Committee on export controls on 3 December.
The reported shipment halt comes amid strong demand for air cargo within Asia. Fred Ruggiero, Cathay Cargo’s Americas cargo chief, told The Loadstar at TIACA’s Air Cargo Forum in Miami that the carrier was looking for more capacity within the region. Another airline executive at the forum pointed to technology shipments from Taiwan and Vietnam as a major source of pressure on space.
Cathay, for example, carried 162,747 tonnes in October, up 7.5% year on year, while its network-wide cargo capacity rose just 0.5%. It cited strong export demand from North-east and South-east Asia, including shipments of network equipment from the south-east, and said semiconductor traffic helped drive growth in its specialist cargo business. An additional A330 freighter operated by Air Hong Kong, under a lease announced in June, is due to serve selected regional routes. Across the industry, IATA recorded a 10.2% year-on-year rise in air cargo traffic within Asia in September.
Meanwhile, South Korea’s semiconductor exports nearly quadrupled in value, year on year, in the first 20 days of November, rising 294.4%, to $38.5bn. Chips accounted for 49.7% of the country’s export value over the period.
However, the traffic is not just one-way; Cathay is carrying server racks in both directions across the Pacific.
“We ship a good number of server racks from Asia into the US, as well as from the US to Asia,” said US-based Mr Ruggiero, although he admitted that “we ship more on the inbound than outbound”.
The rush to build data centres is also putting some of the equipment that powers them on aircraft. A GE Vernova logistics representative told the Miami forum conventional utility projects typically ran on a multi-year timetable. Hyperscalers gave the company less time to manufacture and deliver equipment to site, she said, so it used “a lot more air freight”.
The air cargo industry will be hoping that these suspensions are just that – suspensions – and that all the AI hardware will soon take to the skies again. Preferably, in time to boost what would otherwise undoubtedly be a lacklustre January.

1970 Dodge Challenger R/T SE Hemi Tribute Was Parked in 1987, Restored for MCACN 2026
9 photos
Photo: Geoff Stunkard's Zookeeper's Diary/YouTube
Introduced in 1970, the Dodge Challenger spent only two years on the muscle car market. But that was enough to establish it as one of America's most iconic vehicles from the era. Over 50 years later, the Challenger is a highly desirable classic.
Of course, some old-school Challengers are more sought-after than others. While the base model doesn't get a lot of attention, the R/T version stands out at public auctions. Add a Hemi into the mix, and collectors will throw six-figure sums at it.
The range-topping option in 1970, the 426-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) Hemi is quite rare. Dodge built only 356 units with this powerplant, which is less than 0.5% of all the Challengers built in 1970 (76,935 examples).
It's unclear exactly how many of these Mopars are still around today, but the Hemi Challenger R/T is so desirable that many enthusiasts have built tribute cars. Most aren't all that great, but some are so accurate that you can barely set them apart from the real deal. This green R/T SE that was recently unveiled at the 2026 Muscle Car and Corvette Nationals (MCACN) is one of them.
This Challenger was born as a true R/T SE. The SE stands for Special Edition, which was a luxury and styling trim option. It was available on both the standard and R/T models and included a vinyl top with a smaller "formal" rear window. It also had SE medallions on the C-pillars, leather/vinyl bucket seats, an overhead console, and upscale trim accents.
Records show that Dodge sold 9,976 cars with the SE package, including 3,753 R/T models. Because it was born with a 383-cubic-inch (6.3-liter) V8, which was standard on the R/T, this Challenger is one of 2,522 units made. It was already a pretty rare car when it rolled off the assembly line.
How did it end up with a Hemi? Well, it's not a recent build with a crate engine . This Mopar flaunts a true 426 Hemi. The powerplant found its way into the car in 1981, when the current owner bought it with an empty engine bay. He got a used Hemi V8 and immediately planted it under the hood. Six years later, however, he put the Challenger into storage.
Nearly four decades later, he decided that the Mopar deserved a second chance, and he took it to Apex Automotive. The vehicle was restored to factory specifications, but the 426 Hemi engine was retained. Moreover, the engine bay was detailed to look like this Challenger was actually born with a Hemi.
Had it been a true Hemi Challenger R/T SE, this hardtop would have been one of only 60 units produced. That's the type of production number that comes with a six-figure value exceeding $200,000 in this type of condition. It's obviously not the case here, but this Challenger has to be one of the finest Hemi tribute cars out there.
What's your take on replicas ? Do you think these cars can shine next to the real deal? Check out this Challenger in the video below and let me know in the comments section.

Glencore's business has long been centred around coal. Credit: Glencore
Posted By: Mining.com Staff November 26, 2026
Glencore (LSE: GLEN) has picked Colin Glasenberg, a nephew of former CEO Ivan Glasenberg, to run its coal mines, Bloomberg reported Wednesday.
He would take charge as the company tries to recover lost production at four British Columbia mines that supplied three-quarters of its steelmaking coal in the first nine months of the year.
Glasenberg, who runs Glencore’s oil operations, is due to succeed Earl Melamed in February when Melamed retires, according to Bloomberg , which cited people familiar with the appointment. Glencore still lists Melamed as its head of industrial coal.
Elk Valley Resources mined 16.1 million tonnes of steelmaking coal in the nine months to Sept. 30, down 3.3 million tonnes, or 17%, from a year earlier. That exceeded the 3.2-million-tonne decline across Glencore’s entire steelmaking coal business. Elk Valley’s plants processed less coal and recovered less saleable product as crews opened new mining areas, Glencore said in its production update .
The Canadian mines generated $843 million (C$1.20 billion) in adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization in the six months to June 30. That was 44% of the $1.93 billion Glencore earned on the same basis from all the coal it mined, according to the company’s half-year figures .
Elk Valley
Elk Valley’s output rose 16% in the quarter to Sept. 30 from the previous quarter as plants ran longer after scheduled maintenance. Glencore expects full-year steelmaking coal production near the low end of its 30-million- to 32-million-tonne forecast.
Glencore bought 77% of Elk Valley from Teck Resources (TSX: TECK.A, TECK.B; NYSE: TECK) in 2024 and shelved plans to spin off the coal business after consulting shareholders.
Ivan Glasenberg, who ran Glencore from 2002 to 2021, was its largest shareholder as of Jan. 30, with 1.22 billion shares, according to the company’s annual report . Glencore shares closed Wednesday in London at 432.25p, down 2%. At that price, the January holding would be worth £5.27 billion.
The future of one Elk Valley mine, Fording River, hinges on a proposed extension. Federal and provincial regulators are reviewing the project , which would maintain capacity at 10 million tonnes a year at the mine, about 15 km northeast of Elkford. Elk Valley says the project could add about 35 years to the mine’s life and sustain about 1,500 jobs.
The Idaho Conservation League asked regulators in February to pause the review until water crossing the U.S. border consistently meets the selenium standard for Lake Koocanusa.
“Downstream communities and fisheries should not bear additional risk while existing pollution problems remain unresolved,” the league wrote in its federal submission .

A man in Denver has found a cheap way to beat Waymo’s self-driving system: a few orange traffic cones and a carton of eggs.
Waymo says it has counted at least 30 egg attacks on its robotaxis in Denver, all believed to be the same man. And the Denver District Attorney’s Office has declined to file charges, calling it a civil matter, according to The New York Times .
Box it in, then egg it
The method is laid out in a Denver police report filed last month. The man pulls up in front of a Waymo somewhere in or around downtown, takes orange cones out of his trunk, and sets them around the robotaxi so it can’t drive off. Then come the eggs, sometimes thrown from his driver’s seat, sometimes after he gets out.
He leaves in a silver Toyota Corolla. Per the report, that car belongs to a fleet leased out to Lyft drivers. The man hasn’t been identified, and Lyft didn’t comment.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
A Waymo investigator took seven of the incidents to police. Each egged vehicle had to come out of service for cleaning, and the detailing bill came to about $2,000. No permanent damage.
Police brought their findings to prosecutors, who decided “no criminal charges” were appropriate. A spokesperson for the DA told the Times the office is now collecting evidence on potential damage and will work with the city attorney to find “the most appropriate legal mechanism to make this behavior stop.”
At least one Waymo had a rider inside. Jeff Hunley was headed to the Union Station neighborhood in September when his robotaxi got hit. He filmed it, said he felt safe in the car, and got his fare refunded.
Two months into Denver
Waymo opened its Denver service to the public on September 1 , alongside San Diego and Tampa. The company now runs more than 100 vehicles across 60 square miles of the city, and Mayor Mike Johnston is a fan. He called them popular and affordable, and couldn’t resist adding that “overall they’re a good egg.”
The rest of November hasn’t been as friendly. California’s DMV ordered Waymo’s driverless vehicles off state freeways on November 11 after robotaxis drove into active construction zones and one tried to get past a CHP traffic break. Waymo responded by pausing freeway rides in every US market.
And vandalism isn’t new for Waymo. We covered it when at least five of its I-Pace robotaxis were set on fire during protests in Los Angeles last year.
Why the cones work
Putting a single cone on a Waymo’s hood to freeze it has been a known trick since San Francisco activists did it in 2023. Ringing the car with cones works for the same reason: the Waymo Driver is built to respect them, and it won’t push through.
A human driver getting pelted with eggs would just roll over a cone and leave. A robotaxi sits there and takes it.
That’s the correct default. You don’t want a driverless car deciding when a cone is optional, especially two weeks after regulators pulled Waymo off California freeways for ignoring work zones. But it means anyone with a trunk full of cones can pin a robotaxi in place for as long as they want.
Electrek’s Take
We’ll try to keep the egg puns to a minimum. Mostly.
This is small-time vandalism. Two grand in cleaning, no injuries, no lasting damage. But it shows a real weakness in robotaxis: they’re designed to be the most cautious car on the road, and a determined person can turn that caution against them in under a minute. The car can’t escape, can’t honk its way out, and apparently can’t stop the same guy from coming back 30 times.
The DA’s call is hard to follow. Prosecutors have a repeat pattern, a vehicle tied to a known fleet operator, rider video, and robotaxis that are basically rolling camera rigs. And still no charges. If someone boxed in a regular taxi with a passenger inside and started throwing things at it, we suspect the answer would be different.
At the same time, I can’t help but respect the guy’s dedication.

A simultaneous request by five truck drivers to have their CDLs reinstated after losing them through the change in federal policy regarding non-domiciled drivers is open for comments in the Federal Register, and already has attracted both support and pushback on the possibility.
The request by the five, published in Tuesday’s Federal Register , comes as the industry awaits a court ruling that could overturn the non-domiciled rule implemented earlier this year , with a federal court already having shot down one interpretation of the new policy.
The new non-domiciled rule, published in March, requires the states that issue CDLs to not issue them “unless the applicant provides evidence of lawful immigration status,” according to the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) in recapping the background of the five driver requests.
Each of the five drivers has a different set of details surrounding why they no longer have a CDL under the non-domiciled rule. But they all boil down to their respective ongoing applications seeking to turn a temporary legal situation into a more advanced status not having been completed, resulting in their licenses having been yanked or not extended due to their respective states’ interpretation of the rule.
Telling their stories
For example, applicant Yehonatan Kapach , according to the Federal Register notice devoted to his request, holds an unexpired Employment Authorization Document (EAD), which was issued to him while he has a pending asylum application to remain in the U.S.
His CDL came from North Carolina, where he resides. It was due to expire in July 2028.
But in August, according to the notice, “the North Carolina DMV downgraded Mr. Kapach’s Class A CDL to a class C CDL. He states that the DMV did not offer any explanation of the legal basis for doing so in writing; rather, he was told orally that this was based on his lack of lawful permanent resident status.”
Kapach is asking for a 5-year exemption from 49 CFR 383.71(b)(9), the relevant federal statute, to allow North Carolina to reinstate his CDL.
The other four applicants all have similar stories. One of them, Nikolai Kostarev , in the country legally under asylum laws, is waiting for a green card, but his CDL from Oregon expired in August and he can not get a new one. “Mr. Kostarev indicates that there is no basis in his record to treat him as an unvetted, foreign-domiciled, new driver,” the application says.
Nick Castello is a disabled U.S. Marine Corps veteran. His request is more broadly made for FMCSA to offer relief to those who are in the U.S. legally but not of such a duration that they can get a CDL under the non-domiciled rule. There is little information in the request about his own situation.
Luca Donati had his New Jersey CDL downgraded in February because his legal authorization expires in 2027. He is an Italian citizen in the U.S. lawfully.
Amiran Morchiladze’s application is short on details about his background. But it does say he had his CDL from an unidentified state pulled in August while his residency status is going through the legal process, and “that without relief he may lose his truck, the small business he has been building, and his primary source of income.”
Asking for your opinion
The comments window that was opened in response to the requests found some contributors submitting identical views on all five of the applicants. The window remains open until December 24.
But what it also showed was that within 48 hours, the applicants had a lot of supporters. They also had a lot of critics who did not believe they should receive any sort of dispensation.
A comment from Coyote Creek Transportation, with the name of the submitter not identified, raised an issue that has always accompanied the new rule: how do you know the prior driving record of a non-domiciled applicant?
In the comments for the Kapach request, Coyote Creek said “FMCSA established specific eligibility and documentation requirements for non-domiciled CDL holders. Those requirements should not be bypassed through individual exemptions without compelling evidence that the same level of safety and regulatory compliance can be maintained.”
“I respectfully request that FMCSA deny this exemption and consistently enforce the federal licensing requirements established for all commercial motor vehicle operators,” Coyote Creek said.
Coyote Creek made similar comments across four of the five applicants.
In two of them, the commenter added: “The inability to independently verify an applicant’s prior driving history is a significant issue that must not be overlooked.”
‘I followed the rules’
Driver Dirk Van der Spek commented that he opposed all five requests.
He is a Dutch immigrant who said in his comment that he waited five years for a green card, and drove trucks for more than 20 years, mostly for C.R. England.
“I did it by following the rules, even when that was slow and hard,” Van der Spek wrote.
The amended version of the non-domiciled CDL, Van der Spek said, “finally enforces requirements that were on the books for years, and it has been in effect for only eight months. Granting exemptions now, one driver at a time or for whole immigration categories, would start walking it back before it has had a chance to work.”
Those who were impacted tell their stories
The other side of the argument often came from people who had been behind the wheel but no longer can be as a result of the rule.
In a post in broken English, Harpreet Singh said in commenting on the Donati application that “I was driving truck almost 8 years. This administration canceled my license.”
“My work authorization and license get expired same year and same month but they still canceled it,” Singh wrote. “now I get my C class license and do Uber try you feed my family.”
Donati received similar support in a comment from Tendresse Miafouna (gender not disclosed but Tendresse is generally a female name) who said she was in the same situation as Donati.
“I have Granted Asylum status, and my application for adjustment of status is in process,” Miafouna said. “I have lived in Texas for 9 yrs. My Class A CDL was not expired it was valid until 07/2031 because my I-94 status is “Granted Indefinitely.” Despite this my CDL was downgraded to Class C. I have no tickets, no violations or accidents and never been placed under out-of-service orders.”
What will the courts do?
The irony of the five applications is that they are dropping as the non-domiciled rule’s fate is awaiting a ruling in the case of Lujan vs. FMCSA, which was a multi-plaintiff lawsuit aimed at overturning the FMCSA regulation in the Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia. Lead plaintiff Jorge Rivera Lujan is in the U.S. legally under DACA status.
So far, the fight against the rule has mostly gone in favor of the rule’s opponents.
In the Lujan case, oral arguments have taken place in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia. In those oral arguments, questioning from the bench appeared to be tougher on the FMCSA attorneys than those looking to overturn the rule.
Earlier this month, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit backed the state of New York in its fight to reinstate the loss of some federal funding that was withheld over the state’s issuance of non-domiciled CDLs for a holder whose authorization to stay in the U.S expired before the CDL’s tenure ends.
That decision did not overturn the non-domiciled rule, just the denial of federal funds over the state’s policy. But it could be seen as a court finding fault with some aspects of the non-domiciled rule.
On November 13, the day it was handed down, attorneys fighting FMCSA in two courtrooms over the non-domiciled rule quickly noted to their respective judges what had occurred.
For example, attorneys for California immediately wrote to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia to notify it of the New York decision, as California is fighting the Department of Transportation and FMCSA over the same issue: denial of funds over the state’s non-domiciled policies.
“FMCSA has asserted the same erroneous interpretation of the relevant regulations here, which fails for the same reasons,” California Deputy Attorney General Kristen Kido said in her letter.
And three days after the New York ruling, the plaintiffs in Lujan, which also include the American Federation of State, County & Municipal Employees, and American Federation of Teachers, also wrote to the same court (where their case is being heard) to notify it of the New York decision.
“The Second Circuit’s unanimous holding (in the New York case) that previous CDL regulations
contained no date-matching requirement supports Petitioners’ argument that FMCSA’s professed concern about state noncompliance with such a requirement does not support the Final Rule,” the letter said.

Can the fifth-generation Cadillac Escalade still make headlines even though it is not exactly new anymore? Well, it certainly can. After all, its predecessor still get a touch of the limelight every now and then.
Assembly kicked off at the Arlington facility in Texas in 2020, and four years later, the full-size premium SUV was given a mid-cycle refresh, receiving a new front fascia, new colors, wheels, and a few enhancements on the inside, including the curved 55-inch display. Despite looking similar to the IQ , it does not share its underpinnings, as it is based on the same platform as the Chevy Suburban, Tahoe, and GMC’s Yukon, whereas the zero-emission shares its nuts and bolts with the Hummer EV.
But you already knew that, so we’d better get back on track and put the spotlight on the example pictured in the gallery. This Cadillac Escalade-V came directly from Larte Design’s portfolio. The tuner has given it that sandy look mentioned in the title, stating that this machine is “in a color that nobody else is parking next to you,” and that is correct, especially when you combine it with their carbon fiber bits and pieces.
Part of the Esthete body kit, the extras has been made from carbon fiber, and feature a dry carbon look on the SUV in question. One does not need to be a connoisseur of this model to tell that the vented hood has come from the aftermarket world. The same goes for the grille surround, and the new double-layer splitter that extends on the sides of the OEM bumper.
Photo: Instagram | lartedesign It seems that the side skirts on this Cadillac Escalade-V have also come from Larte Design’s portfolio, and so has the rear diffuser with its multi-fin design, and cutouts for the quad exhaust tips. There is also a roof-mounted wing on deck, as well as wheel arch attachments. The pictured SUV rides on new wheels that appear to have come from Vossen’s portfolio, and they spin around a set of red brake calipers.
This is one Cadillac Escalade-V that easily stands out from the crowd due to its satin sand look and dry carbon components, as well as the new alloys, and several black details, but the question is whether it rocks this look like champ or not. So, where do you stand on that?
Before inviting you to scroll down and leave your impression on this tuned ride, we will remind you that it features a supercharged 6.2-liter V8 engine breathing air from behind that imposing grille. The Escalade-V has 682 hp (691 ps/508 kW ) and 653 lb-ft (885 Nm) of torque on tap, taking a manufacturer-estimated 4.4 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph). So, what’s your take on the pictured Caddy? A FedEx Corp. McDonnell Douglas MD-11 cargo jet overran the runway at Miami International Airport amid heavy rain and thunderstorms, causing the Federal Aviation Administration to issue a temporary ground stop of all flight activity during a busy holiday travel day.
Less than three months ago, an Amazon Air Boeing 767 freighter had a runway excursion at Miami airport, hit a vehicle, crashed through the fence and crossed a road before coming to a stop, resulting in the death of five people and serious injuries to other people.
“A FedEx aircraft overran Runway 26R at Miami International Airport at approximately 8:40 p.m. All runways are closed except for the south runway (9R). Miami-Dade Fire Rescue units have responded, and there are no reported injuries,” the airport said in a statement. There were two pilots on board the aircraft.
The ground stop has since been lifted.
The large FedEx ( NYSE: FDX ) freighter arriving from the company’s global hub in Memphis, Tennessee, missed the target runway’s landing zone, turned slightly left after leaving the runway to avoid a localizer antenna and came to a stop near the airport perimeter fence, according to The Aviation Herald.
“FedEx Flight 910 from Memphis to Miami experienced an issue upon landing Wednesday evening at Miami International Airport. We are grateful that our crew is safe and there are no reported injuries. We are coordinating closely with investigating authorities, and any additional questions should be referred to the FAA,” FedEx said in a statement.
🚨 NEW VIDEO: A closer look at the FedEx cargo plane that overran the runway at #Miami International Airport Wednesday night. The MD-11 was arriving from Memphis when it went beyond Runway 26R and ended up in the grass. The incident prompted an FAA ground stop and forced the… pic.twitter.com/Q9kUpuXkYy — CodeThreeNews (@CodeThreeNews) November 26, 2026
Executives late last month said that most of the company’s 27 MD-11 t r i-engine jets have returned to service after fixing a design flaw that investigators have primarily attributed to the fatal crash last November of an MD-11 operated by UPS.
The MD-11 will likely be idle for an indefinite period to allow for an investigation of the incident and inspect the plane for potential damage. The loss of availability creates a logistics headache for FedEx during the peak shipping season, but the company will likely be able to replace the capacity with reserve aircraft, using an outside carrier or relying more on its truck network.
Why It Matters: Cargo airlines have been involved in a series of accidents at Miami airport in the second half of the year. Earlier this month, A UPS Boeing 767-300 freighter aircraft sustained damage in a low-speed ground collision when the pilots got too close to an intersection and a passenger jet moving towards its gate struck the plane with its wing tip.
The National Transportation Safety Board is still investigating the Amazon Air accident. Amazon’s Boeing 767-300 aircraft was operated by third-party carrier 21 Air.
According to the NTSB’s preliminary report, the crew came in too fast and was unable to extend the flaps to the proper landing position. The plane was above the proper glide slope and when the crew pushed the nose down to get back on the proper glide slope it caused the plane to gain speed. Instead of executing a go-around, the plane touched down long on the runway with one wheel and it took several seconds for the other wheels to touch down. By then, it was too late to stop and the plane rolled past the runway.

By: Northern Miner Staff November 26, 2026
Torex Resources (TSX, NYSE: TXR) is considering two mill upgrades at its Morelos complex in Mexico as part of a plan to nearly double output within five years, according to Red Cloud Securities.
The larger expansion would cost about $100 million (C$142.2 million) and lift processing capacity to 14,500 tonnes a day, Red Cloud mining analyst Ron Stewart said Thursday in a note. A construction decision is targeted for the first quarter of 2028.
An earlier $5-million to $10-million upgrade would remove processing bottlenecks and raise capacity by about 15% by the end of 2027, Torex’s latest earnings presentation shows.
Torex’s Los Reyes gold-silver project in Sinaloa state would provide another source of growth. “Based on a preliminary project timeline, construction of Los Reyes would commence in 2029 with first production in 2031,” CEO Andrew Snowden said in July.
Red Cloud’s Stewart sees a path to an annualized production rate of about 800,000 gold-equivalent oz. by the end of 2031, up from roughly 450,000 for now. The Morelos mine in Guerrero state could supply about 650,000 oz. of that total, with the remainder coming from Los Reyes.
December start
The next milestone is Media Luna North, where Torex expects first ore before year-end, with Stewart anticipating a December start. The company forecasts an average mining rate of about 1,000 tonnes a day in 2027, with further increases toward its design capacity of about 2,300 tonnes a day.
Los Reyes would require an initial $515 million, which Torex expects to fund from Morelos cash flow. The July preliminary economic assessment forecasts annual output averaging 161,000 gold-equivalent oz. during the first 11 years, comprising 111,000 oz. of gold and 3.6 million oz. of silver. The average falls to 134,000 gold-equivalent oz. over the full 14.4-year mine life as lower-grade stockpiles enter the mill. Torex plans a prefeasibility study in 2027 and a feasibility study in 2028.
Torex shares dropped 0.2% to C$64.35 Thursday morning in Toronto, valuing the company at about C$5.8 billion ($4.1 billion). They have traded between C$51.40 and C$85 over the past year.

13 Billion Years Old Galactic Core Called Dún Aonghasa Has Astronomers Scratching Their Heads
6 photos
Photo: ESA
There are things in this Universe of ours that the average human mind will never be able to properly understand. Like, say, a quasar that existed 13.1 billion years ago and had the mass of no less than 360 million suns.
They call it J1504+6252, or Dún Aonghasa, after the prehistoric cliff-top fort on Inis Mór, in Ireland, and it is, by all intents and purposes, the most distant quasar discovered to date. Spotted by the European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope, its light reaches us over the eons from just 630 million years after the Big Bang .
As a reminder, quasars are essentially galactic cores comprising a supermassive black hole, the accretion disk, and jets of energy. As it feeds on the surrounding gas, it releases a tremendous amount of energy, which is what Euclid sees.
Normally, quasars are not forever, and Dún Aonghasa probably turned into a normal galaxy with a black hole at its center a long time ago. The light seen in the images snapped by Euclid has long stopped shining.
The Euclid finding is not important only because it's the most distant quasar ever discovered, but also because it kind of has astronomers scratching their heads at how such an enormous black hole could have existed so close to the Big Bang. There is no answer to that question yet, but the discovery is still young...
The finding announced this week breaks a previous Euclid quasar record, made public a few months back, by no less than 40 million years. It has already been confirmed using a number of other telescopes, including the W.M. Keck Observatory, the Large Binocular Telescope Observatory, the Hubble, and the James Webb Space Telescope.
It is because of Webb that we now know the quasar has a black hole with the mass of 360 million suns at its core to power it.
The Euclid telescope launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket back in 2023, and positioned itself at Lagrange Point 2 (L2), 932,000 miles (1.5 million km) from Earth. In the time it has been active, it found 12 new quasars beyond redshift 7 (about 12.9 billion light-years away). The Dún Aonghasa is the only confirmed one beyond redshift 8.
The studies performed so far on the cosmic object point to it having grown extremely rapidly very early in the life of the Universe, and it is considered a rarity of account of the relatively slow rate in consumes material. According to ESA , this puts pressure on models of early black hole formation and growth, and only time will tell if we'll be able to clear up the mess the discovery has generated.
The main mission of the Euclid telescope is to study dark matter and dark energy and how they impact the visible Universe. It will also try to find a reason why its expansion is gaining speed. To do that, it will generate the largest 3D map of the Universe ever created.
Earlier this month, ESA released the first batch of data from the telescope, 1.7 million GB of it. The release, called DR1-Foundation , includes 13 months' worth of observations, and it'll probably keep astronomers busy for ages to come.

Photo: Cosco Shipping
By Alison Koo
26 November 2026
Cosco Shipping Lines is pushing ahead with one of the industry’s largest newbuilding programmes, seemingly unperturbed by overcapacity concerns.
Currently, Cosco and subsidiary OOCL have ordered 100 vessels, for around 1.46m teu of new capacity, as well as leases for vessels under construction totalling around 500,000 teu, all scheduled for delivery by 2030.
As at 30 September, the self-operated container fleet stood at 610 vessels, with total capacity of roughly 3.66m teu, which are deployed on 458 routes, calling at 676 ports in some 147 countries.
For the first nine months of the year, Cosco Shipping Holdings’ revenue was up 12% year on year, at $28bn, while net profit was up 13%, to $4.65bn.
During an online briefing to shareholders, Cosco representatives said: “Newbuilding decisions are grounded in rigorous analysis of trade trends and long-term capacity planning, not speculative ordering.”
The company cited the key justifications as fleet renewal and modernisation, as environmental regulations tightened.
“More than 22% of the existing global container fleet will be over 20 years old and likely slated for scrapping by 2028–2029. We expect long-term growth in global freight demand to remain intact ,and we also need to ensure supply chain security amid rising geopolitical instability and restructuring of global industrial chains.”
It added that “orderly expansion” helped consolidate its competitive advantages on trunk routes between Asia, Europe, and the Americas, while “providing a stable capacity foundation for exploring emerging markets”.
Management added that Cosco was pursuing “an integrated container shipping + ports + logistics” strategy, and recently opened a regional headquarters in Chongqing to secure cargo from factories there.
On the commercial side, Cosco’s representatives said maintaining long-term, stable customer partnerships remained a cornerstone of its strategy.
They said: “Negotiations for new annual long-term contracts on European routes have begun, while transpacific negotiations typically run between February and April of the following year. Our negotiations are based on market trends and working with customers strengthens our earnings base and resilience against market volatility.”

Surrendering the governance of maritime decarbonisation to fragmented and regional regulations could ultimately prove more expensive for the industry than a globally agreed framework, according to US Federal Maritime Commission chair Laura Di Bella.
Speaking to The Loadstar on the sidelines of the IMO’s Marine Environment Protection Committee (MEPC) in London this week, Ms Di Bella said the US was seeking a global agreement on the IMO’s proposed Net-Zero Framework.
She added: “The regional schemes will ultimately be more costly than something done on a global level. It is harmful, and I believe it when industry says it’s going to be more costly.”
That belief stems from feedback the FMC has been gathering from industry participants, with the message very much stating that regulatory fragmentation would increase costs for shipping businesses.
Noting that the US was “approaching the negotiations in good faith” and wants to reach a global agreement, Ms Di Bella, nonetheless, warned disagreements over the proposed framework’s economic element remained a significant obstacle to reaching a consensus.
Under the proposal, ships that exceed fuel-intensity limits would be charged, with the money going into an emissions pricing and revenue-recycling mechanism that would reward zero-emission fuels.
However, the FMC chair said the mechanism was overshadowing discussions about greenhouse gas reductions, adding that “the economic element needs its own separate discussion, and then [so are] the GHG measures”.
For the US to accede the agreement, Ms Di Bella said, it would need to fit four principal requirements: no economic element; a fuel-agnostic approach; technology neutrality; and clarification over the treatment of emissions trading schemes (ETS).
On the latter, she said the US did not consider the prospect of receiving credits under a future scheme sufficient, calling for the removal of the existing ETS to avoid what she considers “double taxation”.
“We are continuing to engage with the other participants in an effort to bridge these differences, but we believe the economic element has come to dominate at the expense of the environment,” noted Ms Di Bella.
“We need negotiations to be focused on the environmental element. For this reason, if we are to see any progress, the ETS needs to go. It presents an opportunity to not only tax much, which is an issue we have, but then a second time. You cannot have both.”

Japan's 2027 Acura Integra Type S Coming December 2026 With a Six-Page List of Caveats
36 photos
Photo: Honda
The first-ever Acura for Japan is here, with Honda confirming a December 18 launch date in the automaker's home market. Produced in the United States of America, the Integra Type S will ship to the Land of the Rising Sun with the steering wheel on the wrong side for left-hand traffic, an infotainment unit that speaks only English, and climate controls that refuse to use Celsius.
That's not all, though. Per a six-page document listing all caveats, the traffic-sign recognition system of the Integra Type S cannot accurately identify Japanese signs. Just like Toyota, Nissan, and Subaru, the folks at Honda are candid about the compromises associated with a left-hand-drive American vehicle in Japan. The document reads like a checklist of things that will not work as expected.
Japanese customers in the market for the ITS will have to wait until December 18, and Honda is limiting the initial allocation to 250 vehicles. 30 of them will be sold through a lottery system, while 220 others will be handled by dealers. All hail from the Marysville plant in Ohio, and the suggested retail price of the Japanese-market Integra Type S is an eye-watering 8,998,000 yen (including consumption tax).
That's close to 56,500 dollars at current exchange rates, putting the Japanese ITS very close to its American counterpart. Slightly updated for model year 2027, the compact-sized liftback carries an MSRP of 54,600 bucks, plus 1,395 dollars for the destination charge. As ever, it flaunts a 2.0-liter turbo inline-four with 320 ponies to its name, a six-speed manual tranny, and a limited-slip differential.
Honda is bringing the Integra Type S to Japan under a certification framework that makes it straightforward to sell American-built vehicles without going through the domestic approval process. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport, and Tourism introduced it back in February 2026, and this framework essentially deems American vehicles compliant with all relevant Japanese standards.
Photo: Honda Beyond the Integra Type S, other confirmed models for the Japanese market include the Passport TrailSport Elite, Highlander, Tundra, Camry, Ascent, and Murano. Available exclusively for government and certain fleet buyers through the RMA Group, a bunch of Ford trucks are coming to Japan as well.
Although the aforementioned framework removes the need for additional Japanese testing under the normal route, American-built vehicles still need ministerial approval. The American-market headlights of the Integra Type R have had their beam alignment altered for Japanese roads, and the license plate mounting setup is different as well.
Honda further changed the Wi-Fi frequency to comply with domestic radio regulations. Localization efforts, however, leave much to be desired. The driver sits on the left instead of the right, and both the indicator and lighting stalk remain on the left side of the steering column.
Infotainment menus are entirely in English, built-in navigation isn't available, SiriusXM cannot be used, and neither can Acura Link or System Update. Even the clock needs manual adjustment because the built-in software lacks a Japanese time zone setting. Indeed, plenty of compromises here.
The certification system used to bring the ITS to Japan will also be employed for the Passport TrailSport Elite, which is likely coming in the first quarter of 2027. Rather than Ohio, all versions of the US-built Passport are assembled at the Honda Alabama Auto Plant in Lincoln.

source_document.body:
Ocean freight rates remain far above year-ago levels, and relief is likely to be gradual, a new analysis finds, as the market moves from “disruption management” to “transition management.”
Container market rates are up 138% year over year and 15% from August, according to DHL Global Forwarding’s November update, but prices have roughly stabilized at the level of the previous month as peak-season intensity fades. DHL ( DHL.DE ) expects rates to stay “well above last year’s baseline” in the coming months. Ahead of contract season, it says rates are unlikely to match 2025 levels, but they should soften as fourth quarter volumes decline amid the traditional lull.
Global demand is up 5% year to date and 4% year over year; Asian exports are up 8% year to date. DHL describes growth as increasingly uneven — Asian exports and secondary trades are strong while backhauls lag. On the Far East–Europe westbound trade, demand is up 9% year to date, while the backhaul is flat at 0%.
Capacity and congestion
Global container fleet capacity is forecast to grow 4% in 2026, below the roughly 6% annual average of the past decade. More than 10% of the current fleet, or 3.6 million TEUs, is tied up in congested ports, and DHL puts the reduction in effective capacity at about 15%, largely from congestion in Asia after typhoons hit Chinese ports in July and August.
Global net vessel capacity growth is forecast at 4% in 2026, 9% in 2027 and 15% in 2028. DHL says new capacity should exceed nominal trade growth as major carriers have gone on an historic order binge for newbuildings. Scrapping has so far been minimal, but the report warns that “fleet growth does not immediately translate into lower rates.” Terminals, yards and inland transport are limiting the benefit. Weather, geopolitics and hub-and-spoke network models, such as the Maersk (OTC: AMKBY )-Hapag-Lloyd ( HLAG.DE ) Gemini partnership, add to the strain, the analysis states.
Suez return and reliability
After three years of diverted services, more than 60% of Asia–Europe services are again routed via the Suez Canal-Red Sea. Gemini and Mediterranean Shipping Co. are returning fastest, and DHL says carriers in some cases have changed routings in transit without prior announcement. It advises shippers to confirm that cargo insurance covers Red Sea transits, war risks, general average and rerouting. The mix of Suez and diversions around Africa is causing vessel bunching on the Asia–Mediterranean lane, and DHL expects the effect to reach Asia–North Europe in December.
At the same time, schedule reliability has fallen: In key Asian ports, fewer than one in three vessels arrived on time. Clearing the backlog is expected to last through early summer 2027, and DHL also flags possible labor action in Europe.
Fuel costs
Very Low Sulfur Fuel Oil (VLSFO) bunker prices are 69% above the February level and near the 2026 peak, driven by Middle East disruption and uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz. Diesel is up as much as 75% since December 2025, so inland haulage surcharges are expected to remain. The report says shippers can return to a quarterly Bunker Adjustment Factor (BAF), freeze the Q2 BAF with Emergency Bunker Surcharges, or move to monthly bunker updates, which carry no emergency surcharges.
The report was released prior to the Trump administration’s new round of proposed tariffs.
Advice for shippers
DHL recommends that shippers:
Use alternative regional gateways
Accept bookings on a different carrier, even at extra cost
Add buffer time and contingency plans
Build alternatives into rate cards
Importers, exporters, forwarders, and Beneficial Cargo Owners should match their contract approach to each shipment’s needs, DHL recommends, with committed capacity for critical freight, hybrid models for flexible volume, and spot access for unplanned surges.
Why It Matters: Rate agreements don’t guarantee space or schedule reliability, and DHL expects the disruption to push shippers’ focus from price toward resilience.
