The 2027 Concorde Cruiser Atego Motorhome Is a Four-Zone Mansion on Wheels
22 photos
Photo: YouTube/Top Motorhomes
Concorde says that they make motorhomes out of passion, combining decades of experience with only the finest materials and what looks like zero regard for what others might deem "impossible." Their motorhomes are gorgeous landyachts, but even among them, the Cruiser Atego has a place of honor.
Concorde calls it "the powerhouse," designed for living "life like at home." The Concorde Cruiser Atego is a mansion on wheels in the true sense of the word, a four-zone motorhome that checks all the boxes and offers comfortable living on the road for the entire family, regardless of how long the vacation might be.
It's ready for whatever adventure you have in mind in standard configuration, but you can also add extras to make it even better suited for your idea of the perfect RV . That's premium on top of premium, and the money will match – but the experience promises to be unmatched.
Concorde Reisemobile GmbH has been making landyachts since 1981, offering a varied catalog with several series, each divided between several models and, in some instances, different floorplans as well. Once you choose a favorite, you can then proceed to customizing it, either choosing from a given set of options or going all-out with your own take.
Photo: Concorde Reisemobile In between the many available options, though, even the pickiest customer can find something they'll feel is truly theirs. The unit below serves as an excellent example of how elevated, elegant, and packed such a motorhome can be – and all for the price of "just" about half a million euros or about $548,000 for the American reader.
This is the Concorde Cruiser Atego 950 LSRA, the 2027 model year. It's part of the Cruiser Atego series of cabover motorhomes and it's one of three available floorplans, with Concorde describing it as the ultimate family motorhome. Just as good a description would be a yacht in motorhome form, but Concorde is not taking suggestions on that.
Built on the Mercedes Atego 12-ton chassis, it draws power from a 7.7-liter 6-cylinder turbo diesel engine with 229 hp and 1,200 Nm (885 lb-ft) of torque, mated to an 8-speed automatic transmission. This is an RWD motorhome with duallies on the back, and a double-floor construction where Concorde tucks vital components, the holding tanks, and additional storage.
Photo: Concorde Reisemobile The body is built with Concorde Solidtherm construction, so you get aluminum sandwich body panels, double-glazed windows, and a Security Plus entrance door. As options, you can add an awning and hydraulic leveling, so you get more space at camp and the extra time to enjoy it, since setting up will be more efficient.
This floorplan offers sleeping for as many as six people in perfect comfort and, as already stated in the headline, four different living zones, well defined and delimited by physical partitions. You have the kids' bedroom in the cabover, the communal space of the dining room/lounge and kitchen, a spa-like bathroom, and the rear master suite, all arranged in linear fashion since there are no slide-outs to deploy.
The motorhome comes in at 9.62 meters (31.5 feet) of total length, which might not seem like much to the American reader but is actually huge for the European market. Width is 2.5 meters (8.2 feet) and height 3.86 meters (12.6 feet), just a few cm shy of the maximum permitted by law.
Photo: Concorde Reisemobile This floorplan separates the cabin space from the home space in the back through a wood partition – though you can still slide it for easy access. In return, the dining space gets a horseshoe seating arrangement with an adjustable table, so everyone onboard will have a seat at the dining table. At night, the entire dinette converts into a large double bed for overnight guests.
The kids will be sleeping "upstairs" in a cabover bed that comes close to feeling like an actual room. Head height is great, and Concorde adds a pair of opening skylights, removable headrests, lights, and a privacy curtain to make the space nicer than any other cabover bed out there.
From the dining space, you move into the open-plan kitchen , which is divided into two blocks: the main cooking block on the off-side and the fridge, grill, and additional storage on the opposite side. This is a well-appointed kitchen with ample storage space and ample prep space on mineral composite counters, but it's also extremely good looking.
Photo: Concorde Reisemobile Concorde uses natural wood in rich colors, soft-close hinges on all opening doors, and curved, flowing cuts on the cabinetry to create the sense of a space that is functional to use and easy on the eye. It also strives to pack storage even into the tiniest crevice, in what is perhaps a testament to the fact that this is, indeed, a motorhome made for everyday use.
This and the extra space that comes with the larger form factor mean you get everything from a cutlery inset to dedicated recycling trash cans, two slide-out spice racks, a dedicated coffee machine cabinet, and even space for drawer dishwasher. The dishwasher is the rarest of features inside a European motorhome, but you can get it as an option from Concorde.
The bathroom is spa-like. It's also pass-through but without the possibility to use each half independently from the other. In return, you get additional storage space and more movin' and groovin' room, as well as the possibility to use the central part as a changing room .
Photo: Concorde Reisemobile Highlights in here include a plumbed porcelain toilet, a marble-like sink on a vanity with storage, a large corner shower with glass doors, and a full wardrobe with hanging space. Obviously, you also get a power vent and a heated towel rack.
The bedroom at the rear sits higher up than the rest of the motorhome, because Concorde packs a sizable pass-through garage underneath. It comes with a king bed made up of two joined mattresses and has no walkaround space. You do get overhead cabinets, a large opening skylight, and additional storage at the foot of each bed.
The unit shown below, at a recent trade event , also features an optional smart TV in here.
Photo: Concorde Reisemobile Standard features on the Cruiser Atego 950 LSRA include Alde central heating and water heater, a pair of 170Ah gel batteries, a backup camera, and holding tanks with 300, 400 and 400-liter (79, 105, and 105-gallon) capacities for fresh, gray, and black water, respectively. Also standard are soft-walk yacht-like floors and leather upholstery.
Add-ons include a roof-mounted AC unit in the living room, as you can see on the demo unit, a 360-degree camera surveillance system, and extra diesel heating. Concorde also offers upgrades , like lithium batteries (up to 920Ah in total), solar panels (up to 560W), and an inverter.
Photo: Concorde Reisemobile The Cruiser Atego 950 LSRA has a maximum permissible weight of 11,990 kg (26,400 lbs), with approximately 3,305 kg (7,286 lbs) of payload before options. Prices start at €423,950 (approx. $465,300) for the base configuration, with the demo unit below coming with a sticker of €570,085 ($625,700). Or, as Concorde would say , just €570,085.

We're still waiting for used C8 ZR1 prices to fall below MSRP, and while that hasn't happened yet, we're definitely getting closer. We've already seen several examples sell for relatively modest premiums, including a 2027 ZR1 Convertible that fetched just $7,600 over sticker back in September.
In the case of this particular 2026MY ZR1 Convertible, it recently sold for $262,000 at auction, and the original MSRP was $236,760. So roughly $25,000 over sticker, before other expenses. This is still a healthy premium, especially since this car already covered 2,300 miles - good for the seller, it means they drove it instead of just staring at it.
Then again, we are dealing with a fully loaded ZR1 Convertible , finished in Sebring Orange Tintcoat, which might not be my first choice in terms of colorways, but it also wouldn't be my last. The car looks great. Let's put it this way - an outrageous-looking Vette should have a vibrant color.
Other exterior-related highlights include the Carbon Flash dual racing stripes, the carbon fiber high rear wing, front dive planes, hood-mounted Gurney flap, mirror caps, plus the LED headlights, front and rear cameras, and the set of Carbon Flash 20" and 21" forged wheels with Michelin Pilot Sport 4S rubber and carbon ceramic discs with orange-finished calipers. There's also a front-axle lift system, as you'd expect to find on just about any ZR1/ZR1X.
Moving along to the interior, that's where you'll find the Habanero and Jet Black upholstery, carbon fiber trim, heated and ventilated GT2 bucket seats, ZR1 door-sill covers, keyless entry, a performance data and video recorder, dual-zone automatic climate control, cruise control, a Bose sound system, head-up display, a carbon fiber-trimmed steering wheel, and a wide range of electronic driver aids such as lane-keep assist, rear cross-traffic alert, side blind-zone alert, and forward collision alert.
Photo: Bring a Trailer As for performance, we're dealing with a mid-mounted twin-turbocharged 5.5-liter LT7 V8 , pushing 1,064 horsepower and 828 lb-ft of torque to the rear wheels via an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic. According to GM, you can hit 60 mph (97 kph) in just 2.3 seconds behind the wheel of the new ZR1, but that's with a one-foot rollout.
The top speed is even more impressive at 233 mph (375 kph). That's hypercar territory for way less than what you'd pay for something with a more exotic badge. At this point, the only reason why you'd pay for a McLaren or Ferrari is exclusively because of the badge.
Look, value-wise, the ZR1 is a fascinating proposition. But I think I'd rather wait another year or so and see where prices settle. We're already seeing relatively small premiums, so it goes without saying that used models will eventually trade below MSRP. Can you imagine? A 1,064 horsepower Corvette for around $200,000? Honda prepares a new refresh for the Accord sedan, and, thanks to a regulatory filing in China, we now know how it will look. The Accord will get split headlights and a new grille, as well as Honda's redesigned logo. On the powertrain front, the Chinese Accord will gain the trusted hybrid powertrain based on the 2.0-liter gasoline engine that is also sold in the US.
The eleventh-generation Honda Accord is getting a little long in the tooth, which means that it's time for a mid-cycle refresh. The Japanese sedan is not selling as well as it used to, and that's most obvious in China, where this generation hasn't convinced many customers. Sales have dropped sharply immediately after launch, and Honda thinks the design was to blame.
This might explain why the refreshed model tries to address this with a radical makeover, as revealed in a new regulatory filing with China's MIIT. Instead of the classic looks of today, the refreshed Accord will have split headlights, with a narrow strip incorporating turn signals and the daytime running lights. These may be joined by a light strip, but we haven't seen them lit yet, so it's just speculation. The redesigned Accord also adopts Honda's new frameless logo.
There are no notable changes in other areas of the bodywork. The revised model does feature new side skirts and a slightly redesigned rear bumper, but that's about it. The connected taillights continue their career, only this time they integrate the Accord lettering. The Honda logo has been repositioned higher, on the trunk lid.
Photo: GAC-Honda / MIIT filing The MIIT filing doesn't provide pictures of the interior, but it does show close-ups of the Accord's available options. These include a lip spoiler, a pop-up sunroof, as well as several ADAS sensor configurations. According to the document, the updated sedan measures 4,986 mm (196.3 in), thus being 4 mm (0.15 in) shorter than its predecessor. The wheelbase remains unchanged, at 2,830 mm (111.4 in).
The Chinese market also gets a hybrid powertrain sourced from the global-spec Accord, which is also sold in the US. Besides the turbocharged 1.5-liter engine and the 2.0-liter plug-in of the e:PHEV variant, the refreshed model adds a self-charging hybrid based on the same 2.0-liter engine.
The combustion engine develops 146 horsepower and is helped by electric motors and a Li-ion battery supplied by Dalian Taixing Energy. No combined output is stated, but the US-spec Accord e:HEV develops 204 horsepower in a similar configuration. The top speed of the Chinese-market sedan is rated at 198 kph (123 mph).
There's little chance that the refreshed Accord will be offered in the US with similar design changes. Most likely, the US model will continue in its current form until the 12th generation, expected to launch around 2028. This Vintage Wagon-Style French Tiny House Is Specifically Designed for Families
18 photos
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois
One of the things that make the tiny living phenomenon so popular in so many parts of the world is the ability to adapt to virtually every lifestyle and living scenario, from the remote worker’s nomad adventure to the cozy full-time accommodation of a small (or not so small) family. La Bretonne hides one of the best family-oriented layouts, with the added charm of a gypsy caravan style.
All French tiny houses ooze a special kind of charm that can’t be replicated, but the ones that are shaped like vintage wagons are even dreamier. Add to this the benefit of a purpose-built family-friendly layout, and you have one of the best alternatives to an actual house for full-time accommodation. A fine example of that is “La Rouloutte Bretonne”, one of the custom mobile homes by Mon Reve en Bois, an experienced artisan builder operating in Occitania.
The length (7.3 meters/24 feet) and width (3 meters/9.8 feet) are more generous compared to those of a tiny house, while the vintage wagon-inspired roof leads to a naturally lower height of just a little over three meters (10 feet). On the outside, this gypsy caravan-inspired house on wheels looks beautiful, nostalgic, and rustic.
The beauty of natural timber shines through, and it’s no ordinary wood – Mon Reve en Bois is committed to using locally-sourced Douglas pine and spruce from sustainably-managed forests. Apart from its sustainability, this wood is also appreciated on the local tiny house construction market for its naturally high-resin content that makes it almost immune to insects, water damage, and therefore a lot more resilient in the long run.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Before stepping inside the family-friendly layout that makes this French caravan extra special, we need a moment for that beautiful built-in porch. It’s not only an excellent and practical alternative to standard exterior decks, but also a remarkable display of craftsmanship, the kind that defines French tiny homes.
Unlike other models in the same builder’s caravan series, the Bretonne features a full-length front fence, with a side opening instead of a frontal one. Size-wise, it’s a perfect outdoor spot for the morning coffee or simply for watching the sunset. Fully protected by the wagon-style roof, it offers a tiny timber cocoon that can be enjoyed any time of the year – a lovely outdoor extension of the home’s lounge space, boasting the nostalgic charm of traditional porches.
The built-in porch connects to the house via glazed door that serves as the main entrance. This entrance leads into the kitchen, which also includes a lovely dining area, while other the private rooms of the house (two separate bedrooms, plus the bathroom) are cleverly located in the back, for maximum privacy. This way, the kitchen/dining area becomes the main area for social activities, also spilling outside thanks to the connected porch.
French homes on wheels commonly have a compact kitchen, just big enough for daily essentials, and the Bretonne is no exception. Still, it features something that elevates the entire layout: a classic diner-style dining area with a large table and seating on both sides. This dining area and the kitchen are placed facing each other, taking advantage of the layout’s generous width.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Located right next to the main entrance (accessed from the built-in porch), the kitchen displays the typical custom-crafted cabinetry you’d see in a French tiny house – nothing fancy and definitely not luxurious, but built to last, and practical for a small space. A small fridge tucked in a dedicated nook under the counter, a two-burner stove, a range hood, and a microwave oven sitting on an upper open shelf, are the only kitchen appliances, along with a small sink.
Lower and upper cabinets provide essential storage for pantry items and utensils, and a well-placed tiny window ensures proper air circulation. The only downside is the extra-small countertop space, but the dining table can also be used for preparing meals, when needed.
In fact, this beautiful, large dinner table can be seen as a multi-purpose item, turning the dining area into an unconventional home office or even a tiny workshop. A custom-crafted bench on one side, and two chairs on the other side provide generous seating, much more than you’d typically expect in a French tiny house. The entire setup is perfect for a family: a large table, flexible seating, and easy access to the kitchen.
Another window, specifically added for the dining area, makes this little corner even more charming. Yes, there’s no floor space left for a separate, conventional living room with a sofa, but the advantages of a dedicated dining area, big enough for a family, are enough to justify it.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Two separate bedrooms are also unusual for a tiny house, and in this case, it’s one more proof of the generous size being used wisely. The main bedroom is specifically intended for the parents; it’s big enough to house a full-size double bed, it has a large window, and some space left for storage furniture. The second room is ideal for children, because it has bunk beds instead of a regular bed.
Bunk beds are a great way to enhance accommodation capabilities in a small room, and in this case they are even better because kids generally love them. This way, owners can enjoy a remarkably versatile configuration with a main bedroom and a children’s room, both comfortable located on the ground floor (gyspy wagon-style tiny homes like the Bretonne are often preferred for the single-level layout and stress-free access to bedrooms).
The toilet is also located near both bedrooms, offering additional comfort (especially compared to other tiny house layouts, where the bathroom is located at the opposite end), and, although small, is nicely equipped with an enclosed shower cabin, a conventional toilet, and a space-efficient vanity with a very small sink.
Wood paneling throughout this entire tiny house gives it the bohemian, cozy ambiance of a rustic cabin in the woods or in the mountains – folks who appreciate natural living will love the feel of raw timber in every single corner of the house, including the bathroom.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Boasting a total of 22 square meters (237 square feet), this vintage wagon-style tiny house is meant to accommodate up to four people in two separate bedrooms – a truly special perk in the world of tiny living – with the added bonus of a lovely dining area for the whole family. Few homes on wheels offer this kind of separation between the parents’ room and the kids’ room, without having one or more lofts.
Plus, everything featured here doesn’t come with a luxury price tag, which is usually true about most tiny homes built in France. The fully-furnished and equipped version of the Bretonne is priced at less than €50,000 ($55,000) and that’s the kind of bargain you rarely get in the US. Of course, that also has a lot to do with building a tiny house entirely out of wood, inside and out, which is more often seen in European countries like France, Poland, and Germany.
This French house on wheels takes a different approach to family tiny living, using the silhouette and the size of a modern-day gypsy wagon. This builder also offers the option of full off-grid packages with solar energy systems, water tanks, filtration systems, waterless toilets, and wood-burning stoves – it’s up to each owner how far they’re willing to go on the road to natural, sustainable living.

The Nissan Terrano Is Making a Comeback in China, but This Is What America Is Getting
6 photos
Photo: Ministry of Industry and Information China
Nissan is reviving the Terrano nameplate as a boxy, ladder-frame, off-road SUV. Regulatory filings from China's Ministry of Industry and Information have leaked the production model with three distinct powertrain options. The model will not come to America, but Nissan also has something in store for the American market.
Every version of the revived SUV comes equipped with a mechanical, driveshaft-based four-wheel-drive system, shared with the Nissan Navara Pro PHEV pickup truck. That is the model that it also shares the engine lineup, too.
The range starts with the 2.3-liter four-cylinder unit, which delivers 187 horsepower (190 metric horsepower). Higher in the range sits the 2.0-liter inline-four, factory-rated at 254 horsepower (258 metric horsepower).
The plug-in-hybrid variant is the range-topping Terrano, pairing a 204-horsepower (207-metric-horsepower) 2.0-liter turbo gas engine and an electric motor for a combined output of up to 268 horsepower (272 metric horsepower). The official rating of the PHEV has yet to be disclosed.
Photo: Ministry of Industry and Information China The production SUV closely follows the rugged styling of the Terrano PHEV Concept, revealed earlier this year. Expectedly, it will get the boxy styling, with an upright front end, robust wheel arches, heavy cladding, and bold Nissan lettering above the grille. A side-opening tailgate holds the spare tire in typical off-roader fashion.
The model measures 200.7 inches (5,098 millimeters) in length, 77.9 inches (1,979 millimeters) in width, and 77.2 inches (1,961 millimeters) in height, sitting on a wheelbase of 112.2 inches (2,450 millimeters).
The Terrano will ride on 18-inch wheels as standard, but larger 19-inch units will be available at an extra cost. Customers will be able to choose from various trims, spare-wheel covers, and wheel designs and will also have a panoramic sunroof available for the top trim.
The production Terrano is expected to officially debut in China before April 2027. Built in partnership with Dongfeng in China, the model will also make it to Australia, Japan, and potentially India in right-hand-drive form.
Photo: Ministry of Industry and Information China The Nissan Terrano will not set wheels on American soil. The Terrano is produced in China through Nissan’s joint venture with Dongfeng, which makes exports to China widely impossible. However, North America is expected to receive a separate Xterra revival instead.
Xterra is already in development. Once it’s ready, the body-on-frame model will enter production at Nissan’s assembly plant in Canton, Mississippi. Production is scheduled to begin in 2028, putting the rugged SUV on the exact same assembly plant where the previous generation was built before its 2015 discontinuation.
The Xterra will get completely different powertrains. While the Terrano will hit the market with four-cylinder gas, diesel, and plug-in hybrid setups, the U.S.-bound Xterra will feature V6 and V6 hybrid powertrains, compliant with the stricter local emission regulations, CarBuzz reports . The Nissan SUV will give rivals such as the Toyota Land Cruiser and Ford Bronco a run for their money.

By: Northern Miner Staff November 26, 2026
Founders Metals (TSXV: FDR; US-OTC: FDMIF) has extended high-grade gold mineralization deeper at its Antino project in Suriname, where further drilling could help establish the scale of the Froyo zone.
Hole FR298 cut 15 metres grading 23.97 grams gold per tonne from 5094 metres downhole, Founders said Wednesday in a statement. The intercept extended the zone roughly 70 metres down its slope from a previously reported hole, the company said.
Located about 275 km southeast of Paramaribo, Suriname’s capital, Antino covers about 1,024 sq. km. A private airstrip and barges on the Lawa River give crews year-round access. The company gained full ownership of the property in September by acquiring the 30% stake it didn’t own. It also closed a $77-million (US$54 million) investment that raised Gold Fields’ (NYSE, JSE: GFI) stake in Founders to about 19.9%.
“Antino is one of the best, and largest, exploration projects in the Guiana Shield, which Founders is positioned to systematically explore with the strategic backing of Gold Fields (…) and the recent consolidation of 100% ownership,” ATB Cormark mining analyst Nicolas Dion said Thursday in a note.
Pending assays
With the project’s deepest drilling to date now complete, “the next set of results will provide further insight into the scale of the mineralized system,” president and CEO Colin Padget said. Assays are pending from three subsequent deep holes.
The latest intercept extended the Froyo zone about 70 metres down its slope from hole FR230, which returned 9 metres at 12.21 grams gold per tonne in results announced June 23. The zone remains open at depth, and assays are pending from three subsequent deep holes. One of those, FR308, reached 884 metres downhole, the deepest hole yet at Upper Antino.
“We see a high-grade, multi-million-ounce project emerging at the most advanced target (Upper Antino), while the rest of the Antino property hosts the potential for separate discoveries,” Dion said.
Founders shares dropped 0.4% to $6.82 Thursday morning on the TSX Venture Exchange, valuing the Vancouver-based explorer at about C$982 million. They jumped 21% Wednesday after the drill results were released.

By Ian Putzger Americas correspondent
26 November 2026
After a spell in the doldrums, the US warehousing sector has caught a fresh tailwind – with AI a key factor, promising lasting demand.
And Prologis is in expansion mode: the logistics real estate powerhouse is set to break ground on a 1m sq ft warehouse in the Chicago area, a single-storey, cross-dock building with a 40ft clear height and 290 parking spaces.
A second development in the area will follow; Prologis recently acquired a 26-acre lot where it intends to create 454,00sq ft of warehousing.
And its appetite for expansion is not confined to the US market. In August, Prologis signed an agreement to acquire UK-based warehousing firm Segro for about $18.8bn, a deal expected to close in the first half of next year, to create a player in Europe with about $269bn in assets, covering 368msq ft of space.
The warehousing sector limped through last year as the headwinds from Washington’s tariff policy took the wind out of its sails, just as a large chunk of new warehousing space was coming into the market. Occupied floor space shrank, due to economic uncertainty and slower economic growth, pushing net absorption well below the 2m sq ft average seen in previous years.
However, the latest edition of the Industrial Business Indicator, which Prologis publishes quarterly, shows a much improved picture.
The index, which is based on a customer survey, averaged a reading of 59.5 in Q3, followed by 59.4 for October. According to Prologis, this indicates an extended peak season and robust growth in the flow of goods, prompting expansion of logistics users’ activities. The absorption of logistics space hit 63msq ft in the third quarter, sustaining the growth rate registered in the first half.
Vacancy rates fell ten basis points, and are expected to decline further in the new year, given current leasing and pipeline activity, according to Melinda McLaughlin, SVP and global head of research.
“Scarcity is beginning to emerge in a growing number of locations and size categories as new deliveries are roughly 20% lower than typical,” she said. “In some markets, data centre development is adding competition for land, power, materials, and workers, which can make new logistics space harder and more expensive to build.”
Indeed, a recent research paper, produced by Prologis Research, noted that “companies building and supporting data centres are creating new demand for logistic space, from equipment makers and suppliers to contractors and logistics providers”.
Logistics real estate firm Cushman & Wakefield corroborated this. Jason Price, head of Americas logistics & industrial research, noted: “Data centre development is creating a physical supply chain that extends well beyond the campus itself. Servers, power and cooling equipment, construction materials, and replacement parts all have to be manufactured, stored, and distributed, and that is now showing up as a meaningful new source of industrial leasing.”
Data centre-related users accounted for 25% of US leases for properties over 1m sq ft signed this year, said Cushman & Wakefield. And Prologis Research forecasts 150m sq ft or more of leasing associated with data centre development through the end of the decade.
Moreover, demand from this segment is durable, it pointed out.
“While nearly all demand will be needed for five or more years, we estimate 50% of generated demand and related jobs will be truly permanent, needed for ongoing maintenance, equipment replacement and upgrades,” wrote Prologis researchers.
AI-related traffic may have replaced e-commerce as the chief engine of global airfreight, but the latter still figures prominently in warehousing demand. In the first nine months of the year, it accounted for 21% of new leasing activity, while advanced manufacturing and data centre support reached 17%, Prologis Research found.

By Charlotte Goldstone
26 November 2026
Criminals posing as truck drivers and dispatchers are infiltrating US haulage firms to steal shipments, with data centre hardware and metals among the most sought-after commodities this year.
In its Thanksgiving cargo theft warning, Verisk CargoNet said criminals were exploiting staff shortages and holiday absences to gain access to carriers’ internal systems.
The intelligence company said the fraudsters were responding to job ads posted by trucking companies and, once hired, gained access to corporate email and telephone systems, allowing them to bid for shipments in the carrier’s name and then steal the freight.
In most cases investigated by Verisk CargoNet, carriers had recruited drivers or dispatchers online without ever meeting them.
The average documented value of stolen shipments in the nine months to September reached $448,456, up 72% year on year.
Truckloads of metals and enterprise computing hardware used in data centres remain attractive to criminals, particularly fully assembled server racks, networking equipment, graphics processors, and memory chips.
Verisk CargoNet recorded 252 cargo theft incidents across five Thanksgiving holiday periods between 2021 and 2025, an estimated $23.9m in stolen goods.
Source: Verisk
While incidents fell from a five-year peak of 79 in 2024 to 58 last year, the figure was still double that recorded in 2021. The Tuesday and Wednesday before Thanksgiving and the Monday after accounted for 62% of incidents, with California, Illinois, and Texas collectively accounting for 56% of reported thefts.
Historically, food and beverages have been the most frequently targeted commodities over the holiday, followed by household goods and electronics.
However, increasingly sophisticated identity fraud is adding to the risks posed by more traditional thefts from unattended trucks and trailers. Criminals are compromising carriers’ email accounts, purchasing carrier credentials, and deceiving hauliers into diverting shipments to alternative delivery locations.
Keith Lewis, VP of operations at Verisk CargoNet, said: “The groups behind these schemes are patient, and they plan around the calendar. A carrier’s email address and phone number are how brokers know who they are dealing with. Guard access to them the way you guard the keys to your trucks.”
Verisk CargoNet urged shippers, brokers, and carriers to increase security and verification measures, while recommending that employers meet prospective recruits, conduct thorough background and reference checks, and validate contact information.
Mr Lewis also called for greater collaboration, urging: “No single shipper, broker, or carrier can see the whole picture, and the criminals count on that.
“When one company spots a suspicious load, a fake dispatcher, or a cloned carrier and reports it quickly, everyone can benefit.”

Contrast Kings: 5 Muscle Cars That Look Awesome With White Vinyl Roofs and Decals
16 photos
Photo: Mecum Auctions
Back when vinyl tops were a popular feature, some customers went with white ones and matching decals which, paired with a contrasting paint color, made already great-looking muscle cars look even better.
Apart from insane performance, the golden age of muscle cars remains arguably the most exciting era in American automotive history because of the timeless styling and factory customization options that were offered back then.
Among those options were the white vinyl top and white decals which, paired with the right exterior color, dramatically improved the elegance of some models.
While white vinyl tops and decals were available on many performance models from that exciting era, the following five pulled off that elegant contrasting look better than anything else roaming the streets.
1968 Dodge Charger R/T Photo: Mecum Auctions The Charger started life in 1964 as a upscale coupe with a dramatic fastback roofline, one that was developed specifically to rival AMC’s popular Marlin .
While the model did succeed in outselling its rival, for the 1968 model year, Dodge completely redesigned the car and moved it from the affordable personal luxury coupe segment to muscle car territory.
The second-generation Charger was available in a tame yet affordable base specification, but the main attraction was the performance-oriented R/T (Road and Track) trim.
Photo: Mecum Auctions When this option was chosen, the Charger got a potent standard V8 or an optional one with even more oomph, such as the range-toping 426 HEMI .
The R/T came with a rear stripe package, which could be ordered in white. A vynil top was also available and optionally, it could be delivered in white instead of black.
With the white top and stripes, plus an eye-catching primary color such as Matador Red, the 1968 Dodge Charger R/T looked aggressive, yet also extremely elegant.
1968 Chevrolet Chevelle SS 396 Photo: Mecum Auctions Like most iconic muscle cars from the 1960s and 1970s, the Chevelle SS started out as a performance package, then morphed into a standalone performance model starting with the 1966 model year.
The Chevelle, including the SS performance model was available with a vinyl top for two-door hardtops from 1966. However, with the debut of the redesigned second-generation for 1968 model year, a white vinyl top option was added.
As you can see in these images, the white top, paired with the SS-exclusive white stripes and a contrasting primary color worked wonders on the already-gorgeous Chevelle SS, adding elegance to its naturally aggressive styling.
Photo: Mecum Auctions Like its immediate predecessors, the 1968 Chevelle SS came with a standard 396-ci (6.5-liter) big-block V8 rated at 325 hp (RPO L35). But if that wasn’t enough, customers could choose one of the two optional high-output 396s rated at either 350 hp ((RPO L34) or 375 hp (RPO L78).
Regardless of the engine it was equipped with, the 1968 Chevrolet Chevelle SS 396 was an iconic muscle car that thrilled with its straight-line performance and its timeless styling.
While any exterior color, vinyl top and decal combination looked great, the white top and decals contrasted by a vibrant exterior finish made this legendary muscle car turn even more heads.
1969 Chevrolet Camaro SS Photo: Mecum Auctions Surprisingly, GM brands took several years to come up with an answer to Ford’s Mustang, which sold like hotcakes since its debut in April 1964.
About two and a half years after the ‘Stang’s memorable New York World Fair debut, Chevrolet finally unveiled its first pony car in the shape of the Camaro.
With gorgeous styling and a wide range of options, including serious performance trims, the original Camaro went toe-to-toe with the Mustang and, although it never outsold its rival, it still became one of Chevrolet’s most revered models.
Photo: Mecum Auctions The first-gen Camaro entered its last year on the market in 1969 and it was offered with more options than ever before.
Among those options were, of course, white vinyl roofs for hardtop variants, including the high-performance SS, which could also be ordered with matching white hockey stripes.
As standard, the 1969 Camaro SS was powered by a 350-ci (5.7-liter) small-block rated at 300 hp, but customers could choose an optional 396, which was available in three distinct output variants, ranging from 325 to 375 hp.
However, when equipped with a white vinyl top , white stripes and a contrasting color, the 1969 Camaro SS looked incredibly good, regardless of the engine stuffed between its shock towers.
1970 Plymouth GTX Photo: Mecum Auctions For the 1967 model year, Plymouth introduced a new sub-model called GTX to the Belvedere range.
Available as a two-door hardtop or convertible, the GTX offered premium options and potent engines, instantly becoming one of the most impressive gentleman’s muscle cars.
While the Road Runner , it’s cheaper, no-frills performance sibling became way more popular following its debut for the 1968 model year, the GTX continued to be available as a premium, upscale muscle car.
Photo: Mecum Auctions For the epic 1970 model year, the GTX received a thorough styling refresh that included redesigned front and rear ends, a new hood on selects engine options and a new strip package, which could be ordered in white or black.
A vinyl roof was available as an option, one which most customers went for. However, a few customers went for the white vinyl roof and matching decals, combined with a primary color from the High Impact palette, which resulted in one of the most beautiful muscle cars that money could buy.
As you can see in the images above, a 1970 GTX finished in the High Impact color called “In Violet Metallic” looked absolutely amazing when combined with a white top and matching stripes, regardless if it was powered by the standard 440 cu in (7.2-liter) Super Commando rated at 375 hp, the optional 390-hp 440 Six-Barrel, or the range-topping, 425-hp 426 HEMI.
1970 Oldsmobile 4-4-2 Photo: Mecum Auctions While Pontiac is widely credited with kickstarting the muscle car craze in 1964 when it introduced the GTO, GM siblings Oldsmobile was the first brand to come up with an answer in the shape of the Cutlass-based 4-4-2.
The original 1964 4-4-2 wasn’t as epic as the GTO, but thanks to Oldsmobile’s tireless effort to improve it, the muscle car became a legend in the years that followed .
Perhaps the most impressive iteration of the 4-4-2 was offered during the memorable 1970 model year when it received a potent, 365-hp 455-ci (7.5-liter) Rocket V8 which could be made even more powerful with the addition of the W-30 performance package.
Photo: Mecum Auctions With or without the W-30 option, the 1970 4-4-2 was one of the most epic performance rides of the year and one of the greatest gentleman’s muscle cars ever created.
The epic model looked extremely well in any available color and decal combination. However, when equipped with a white vinyl top, matching side and hood stripes and a vibrant primary color, it looked even better.
